overview: This file documents U.S. State and War Department efforts between August and October 1946 to restore and regulate communications with occupied Japan. One group of papers concerns commercial telegraph traffic routed through the United States between Japan and Pacific military bases, including proposed and final rate schedules for ordinary, code, deferred, night-letter, VLT, and EFM services. A second group proposes allowing censored commercial correspondence between Allied and Japanese firms to stimulate exports while retaining SCAP control over production, contracts, and foreign trade. The papers trace interdepartmental review, successive cable drafts, and the transition from tightly controlled occupation commerce toward freer competitive trade.

subfiles.title: Memorandum from Martin to Hilldring on telecommunications with Pacific bases
subfiles.about: The memorandum seeks approval of a cable authorizing commercial telegraph service through the United States between Japan and specified Pacific military bases.
subfiles.summary: Martin reports approved rates for Pacific-base telegraph service (Papeete, New Caledonia, Suva, Samoa) at 10-30 cents per word via San Francisco, keeping existing Japan-U.S. rules.

subfiles.title: Whitman memorandum proposing commercial mail with Japan
subfiles.about: Whitman proposes using censored commercial correspondence between Allied and Japanese firms to stimulate Japanese exports.
subfiles.summary: Whitman's draft proposes a Trading with the Enemy Act exemption for non-transactional correspondence on approved exports, preserving censorship; private sample exchanges could yield tentative deals, with importers submitting dollar offers via USCC and SCAP retaining final control, pending FEC approval.

subfiles.title: Easton routing note returning commercial-mail papers
subfiles.about: Easton returns material to Whitman in response to a request.
subfiles.summary: Routing note records returning commercial-mail papers from Easton to Whitman, dated September 1946.

subfiles.title: Socks memorandum returning the proposed commercial-mail cable
subfiles.from: Lieutenant Colonel Hugh G. Socks, Acting Executive, CAD
subfiles.about: Socks returns the proposed cable on commercial mail with Japan following a telephone conversation with Lieutenant Colonel Dice.
subfiles.summary: Civil Affairs Division returns the proposed commercial-mail cable at Easton's request, following a phone call with Dice.

subfiles.title: Draft cable to SCAP on commercial mail and export promotion
subfiles.about: The draft asks SCAP to consider permitting controlled commercial correspondence between Allied and Japanese firms as a means of expanding exports.
subfiles.summary: Draft proposes exempting non-transactional export correspondence from the Trading with the Enemy Act, with censorship and exclusion of objectionable firms retained; sample exchanges could set tentative deals via Boeki Cho, with USCC handling dollar offers and SCAP judging suitability and prices, easing transition to competitive trade.

subfiles.title: Outgoing War Department message on VLT and EFM services
subfiles.about: The message reports where VLT and EFM services from Japan are available and supplies the applicable message and per-word rates.
subfiles.summary: RCA and Mackay confirm VLT/EFM service unavailable to New Caledonia, Papeete, Samoa, Suva but available to seven other Pacific destinations, with full rate schedules given.

subfiles.title: O'Sullivan memorandum requesting concurrence in Pacific-islands cable
subfiles.to: Colonel R. H. Chard, Executive Officer, CAD
subfiles.about: O'Sullivan asks the Civil Affairs Division to report War Department concurrence or requested changes to an attached cable for SCAP.
subfiles.summary: O'Sullivan asks War Department to concur promptly in a draft cable on Pacific-islands telecommunications; a note records CAD notified of concurrence October 16.

subfiles.title: Routed draft cable to SCAP on telecommunications rates
subfiles.about: This routed draft reports the availability and rates of VLT and EFM service between Japan and several U.S. or Pacific destinations.
subfiles.summary: Draft states VLT/EFM unavailable to four Pacific destinations but available to seven others, with EFM at 60 cents per message and listed VLT rates.

subfiles.title: Clean draft cable from War to SCAP on VLT and EFM service
subfiles.about: The draft provides service-availability findings and detailed rates for VLT and EFM traffic originating in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Clean draft cable confirms VLT/EFM unavailable to four destinations, available to seven others with per-message EFM and night-letter VLT rates, drafted by Cansler.

subfiles.title: Annotated duplicate draft cable from War to SCAP
subfiles.about: This annotated duplicate repeats the proposed VLT and EFM service and rate information for Japan's communications with Pacific and U.S. destinations.
subfiles.summary: Annotated duplicate draft repeats the VLT/EFM service distinctions and rate schedule, routed among A-H, JK, and O'Sullivan.

interest: Shows occupation telecommunications policy tying censorship to Japan's trade recovery, through State-War-SCAP-FEC negotiations and detailed tariffs.
